article.summary: Buzz is a self-hostable collaboration workspace whose agent-memory slice is NIP-AE: encrypted per-agent/owner engrams, a memory CLI, and ACP session-time core-profile injection. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark result.

who_what.text: The official README identifies Buzz as built by Block, Inc. and describes this repository as the relay and mobile client, with the desktop app in a separate repository. This review focuses on its NIP-AE agent-memory feature.

architecture.text: NIP-AE represents a core profile and named memory values as kind 30174 addressable events. A JSON body is encrypted with NIP-44 v2 under the symmetric agent-owner conversation key; the agent signs the event, while HMAC-derived d tags conceal the slug from passive observers.

The core crate is an I/O-free implementation of slug validation, cryptographic addressing, encryption/decryption, event validation, and head selection. The CLI connects those primitives to configured relays; ACP separately fetches the core record when a new session is created.

Memory bodies contain one slug and a string or null value; the reserved core body contains a free-form profile. The core profile can use wiki links to refer to other slugs, while this protocol version leaves structured provenance and trust fields out of scope.

behavior.text: The CLI exposes ls, get, hash, set, patch, and rm. Writes create encrypted and signed replacement events with increasing timestamps. Patch checks a SHA-256 preimage before applying a unified diff; a relay response that says a newer head already dominates the write is reported as a conflict.

Removal of a memory slug publishes a value:null tombstone; the CLI refuses removal of the core slug. Optional NIP-09 deletion requests may target old events, but whether relays honor them is relay policy, so tombstoning does not establish historical erasure.

Reads validate the event envelope, decrypt the body, and ensure the body slug derives to its public d tag. Listing groups valid results by slug and selects the head. Relay-side event limits can make listing incomplete because Nostr does not specify pagination.

ACP performs a bounded core query at new-session creation. A valid core becomes prompt text; an empty result is treated as confirmed absence and yields an onboarding nudge, while transport, parse, or unreadable-event errors are logged and inject no section. The fetch does not block session creation.

The relay checks authenticated identity for filters capable of matching agent engrams. Access is restricted to the agent author or addressed owner, with an explicit-ID filter exception documented in the handler. This is source evidence, not an isolation workload result.

metrics.evidence: Named reads, listing and ACP core injection are implemented; no answerability probes were run.
Patch applies a diff under a SHA-256 compare-and-swap guard, but no correction/staleness adjudication was run.
In-band tombstones and optional relay deletion requests exist; no relay-history or post-delete probe was run.
Agent-owner addressing and relay authorization are visible in protocol/code; no cross-owner isolation workload was run.
Signed authorship is visible, while optional source text is not verified attestation; no claim-support evaluation was run.
Relay queries, decryption, head selection and best-effort post-write verification are source-visible; no timing was collected.
ACP injects the core profile at session creation; no token or provider-cost measurement was collected.
Replaceable encrypted relay events and optional tombstone/deletion semantics are documented; no storage measurement was collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded review of NIP-AE and selected CLI, ACP, core, and relay paths at the pinned head. Buzz was not run, and no memory quality or performance result is available.
Nostr listing can be incomplete when relays cap events. Writers can disagree across disjoint relay sets or partitions, and post-write verification is best effort rather than a global transaction.
Encryption does not hide the public agent-owner relationship, prove remembered content is true, or establish relay erasure. The rest of the large collaboration platform was not assessed.

benchmark.text: Benchmark status is not_run. No Buzz system execution, benchmark workload, or tests were run; the project fixture and metric definitions are protocol artifacts rather than results.
